Buick Electra Leaks Online: This Is What You're Missing, America!
7 photos
Photo: Buick China
The first photos of the upcoming Buick Electra GS PHEV sedan hit the internet and you can’t but sit and wonder: why in the world isn't General Motors building this sedan in the United States for its home market?
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) has leaked the official product images and filing data for the upcoming Buick Electra GS plug-in hybrid sedan. Developed by the SAIC-GM joint venture, the large, fastback-style sedan is tailored specifically for the Chinese market and is very unlikely to ever set wheels on American land due to regulatory hurdles and prohibitive tariffs.
The production version represents a significant departure from the much taller, hatchback-like Electra GS Concept that made its debut in April 2025 as a preview of a future production model. And this is it! It may not be the concept car’s identical twin, but it is the next best thing.
With styling that pays tribute to Buick’s iconic Gran Sport lineup, the Electra GS PHEV car features ultra-slim, C-shaped LED headlights linked by an LED strip. The Buick tri-shield logo sits right below on a less aggressive "shark-nose" front fascia.
Photo: Buick China The Electra comes with a sleek, sporty, fastback roofline and streamlined silhouette, while the rear end gets taillights that stretch from one side to the other of the liftgate before curving inward, a layout that sends Aston Martin DBX and Lamborghini Urus vibes.
The Electra GS is the slightly shorter and potentially more affordable alternative to Buick’s existing Electra L7 Sportback sedan. It measures 190.0 inches (4,980 millimeters) in length, 75.4 inches (1,915 millimeters) in width, and 58.9 inches (1,495 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 112.8 inches (2,865 millimeters). Those numbers make it slightly smaller than the Buick Electra L7.
The leaked documents confirm the plug-in hybrid setup, which combines the electric motor, good for 221 horsepower (224 metric horsepower), with either the naturally aspirated 1.5-liter or the turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-four. The naturally aspirated engine produces 72 horsepower (73 metric horsepower, while the turbocharged unit churns out 154 horsepower (156 metric horsepower).
The base variant rolls off the production line with 318 horsepower (322 metric horsepower), while the range-topping turbocharged example sees the light of day with a combined system output of 375 horsepower (380 metric horsepower).
Photo: Buick China The car is equipped with a Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery pack, produced in-house by SAIC-GM Powertrain Technology. However, GM has yet to disclose its capacity and how far the PHEV sedan can drive on electric power only.
GM hasn’t revealed any pricing details either, but it will most likely happen closer to the launch date set for early 2027.
While the Buick Electra GS PHEV will stay away from the U.S., it has every chance to make it to the European market.
